title: Signal refresh and compact trace playbook
content:
Purpose and TL;DR:

This doc is a pragmatic sprint kit for doing a focused "signal refresh" across inference runtimes: prune low-value dashboard panels, standardize a compact set of metrics for token-path investigation, and adopt a lightweight trace sampling strategy that is cheap and operator-friendly. Goal: reduce dashboard noise by ~40% and cut trace query costs while keeping 95th/99th latency investigation fidelity.

Why now:
- Observability has accreted many one-off panels and high-cardinality metrics over the last 18 months.
- Cost and query latency are trending up during spikes (see linked probe-cost note).
- New Dedicated and Private customers demand predictable troubleshooting flows that don’t require deep-dive query gymnastics.

Scope for a single 2-week sprint:
1) Signal catalog cleanup for inference token-serving metrics (compact set defined below).
2) Dashboard pruning: move low-signal panels to an ‘archive’ board and keep one compact operator view per service.
3) Tracing policy change: implement adaptive sparse sampling + mandatory on-demand full traces for specific error classes.
4) Instrumentation checklist for any metric additions going forward.

Non-goals:
- Re-instrumenting models. This is a telemetry-level clean-up only.
- Full SLO rewrite (we will surface candidate SLOs but not finalize).

Compact metric set (names and short defs) - required for each inference service panel:
- token_throughput_total_per_min: token production rate aggregated by model_version and route. Unit: tokens/min. Use for capacity signal.
- request_count_success: number of successful inference requests. Tag by route, tenant_tier.
- request_count_error: count of error responses (4xx/5xx) split by error_class (timeout, mem_error, model_error).
- time_to_first_token_ms_p50_p95_p99: quantile series for TTF token.
- time_to_last_token_ms_p50_p95_p99: request completion quantiles to catch slow paths.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: percent of requests served with cold vs warm KV cache (session / tenant).
- batching_efficiency: effective batch size median and p95.
- operator_query_cost_estimate: synthetic metric approximating dashboard query cost (backfilled if unavailable).
- warm_start_ratio: fraction of requests where model state/prefix cache was present.

Each metric must have: owner, description, unit, tag keys allowed (max 5), backfill-acceptable-flag. Put those as annotations in the metric catalog (see linked confluence).

Tracing guidance - compact trace playbook:
Principles:
- Traces should be signals for investigation, not a continuous stream.
- Keep span shapes predictable: infrastructure spans (container, gpu-device, kernel-launch) should be distinct from model spans (token-gen, kv-lookup, attention-compile).
- Make session_id and tenant_id first-class trace attributes for sessionization.

Span boundary suggestions (names we should standardize on):
- span.inbound.http_receive (lightweight)
- span.router.route_lookup
- span.batch.coalesce
- span.kv.cache_lookup (annotate hit/miss)
- span.model.prepare_weights
- span.model.token_generate (split by chunk if multi-step)
- span.kv.commit_prefix (if writes occur)
- span.outbound.response_send

Sampling policy (proposal):
- Baseline sparse sampling: 0.5% of successful requests sampled across all services (uniform reservoir) for long-term stats.
- Error-triggered full trace: sample 100% when request_count_error increments for error_class in [timeout, mem_error, model_error].
- Heavy-path raise: for services where time_to_first_token_ms_p95 > threshold (TBD), bump sampling to 5% for 10 minutes.
- On-demand pull: operators may request a temporary full-trace toggle for a given tenant_id via a short-lived dashboard button (token-limited role).

Trace payload minimization rules:
- Strip big prompt/text fields from exported spans by default; instead include prompt_digest (sha256 or mmh3) and a prompt_length tag.
- PII/PHI redaction policy: any span with tag contains_personal_data=true should be gated and sent only to private retention tiers.

Dashboard pruning checklist (operator compact view):
- Keep <= 12 widgets in the compact operator board. Prioritize: throughput, ttf p95, request errors, kv_cache_hit_rate, batching_efficiency, model_version_heatmap, operator_query_cost_estimate.
- Archive panels older than 6 months with no edits and < 50 weekly queries.
- Replace freeform JSON widgets with templated metric widgets that have documented metric contracts.
- Add an operator-facing quick-actions row: cold-start probe trigger, snapshot trace fetch, tenant rate-limit toggle (links to internal APIs).

Operational runes and how to investigate a slow-requests alert:
1) Alert fires for time_to_first_token_ms_p95 spike.
2) Check compact board for kv_cache_hit_rate and batching_efficiency. If kv_hit down & batch size down -> likely cold starts.
3) Pull recent sparse traces (last 5 at baseline sampling); if none show the error, toggle on-demand full traces for the implicated tenant_id for 10m.
4) If traces show GPU memory pressure (span.model.prepare_weights slow + mem_error tags) -> page infra-sre and start failover.

Instrumentation guardrails (for reviewers and PR owners):
- New metric PRs must include: owner field, intended dashboard(s), tag cardinality estimate (max distinct values), retention tier recommendation, and a backfill plan if deployed retroactively.
- No new high-cardinality label without an expiration policy (e.g., ephemeral_request_id must be scrubbed within 24h).
- Default histogram buckets for latency: [1ms, 5ms, 10ms, 50ms, 100ms, 500ms, 2000ms, 10000ms]. Use quantile rollups only for dashboards.

Sprint tasks (sample ticket list):
- OBS-5121: build compact operator dashboard template and migrate 6 pilot services. Assignee: Lina.
- OBS-5122: implement adaptive-sparse-sampler in tracing agent v2 and add operator toggle. Assignee: Marcus.
- OBS-5123: metric-catalog annotations and backfill scripts for compact metric set. Assignee: Aisha.
- OBS-5124: dashboard archive process (automation to move panels older than 6 months). Assignee: Tom.

Metrics and trace KPIs to measure success (2-week window):
- dashboard_query_cost reduction >= 30% (measured by operator_query_cost_estimate).
- average dashboard widgets per operator board <= 12.
- trace storage reduction >= 25% while maintaining investigation hit rate (operator satisfaction survey).

Open questions and risks:
- Precise sampling percentages (0.5% baseline) need simulation against production request volumes; could under-sample tail failure modes.
- On-demand full-trace toggle must have RBAC and auditing; otherwise risk over-collection.
- Some existing dashboards are customer-facing and cannot be pruned without customer comms. Need a list and notification plan.

Next steps (today -> sprint start):
- Review plan with eng-observability and SRE leads; get buy-in on trace sampling policy (schedule 30m sync).
- Lock compact metric contract fields on confluence and generate catalog annotation PR.
- Create the four tickets above and schedule owner check-ins.

Notes to self / fragments for follow-up:
- Consider running a query-cost simulator: feed historical dashboard queries and estimate cost with pruned widget set.
- Add example curl for on-demand toggle API in ops runbook.
- Put a one-page customer comms template under "shared_drives/company/misc" if we need to notify customers about visible dashboard pruning.

If you want to pair on the migration of the first two services this sprint ping me in #observability (Aisha) or drop into my calendar.
